aggregation: frame-index aligned: every plotted point is a raw per-frame value, no time interpolation (time-interpolation over 12 mismatched non-uniform axes produced a resampling-artefact sawtooth)
x_axis: dt = physical_time - t[9] of the same trajectory, where t[9] is the LAST OBSERVED INPUT frame; this matches the paper's lead-time convention. The x-axis is pinned to start at 0 via xlim; the drawn curves begin at the first predicted frame (dt = 1.0 Myr on GeoSim-Plume1). A zero-error anchor at dt=0 is deliberately NOT added: it is not drawable on a log axis and renders as a spurious vertical drop to the axis floor
why_t9: the first version used t[10] (first predicted frame) as the origin. That differs from the frozen protocol by exactly one time step (1.0 Myr on GeoSim-Plume1, 0.098-1.0 on GeoSim-Plume2), so a reader taking a value off the figure at dt=12 was reading the paper's lead-13 number. Author ruling 2026-09-26: match the protocol.
full_panels: 6 fields x 2 subsets, seed and trajectory bands kept
boundary_note: computed per trajectory as t[19] - t[9], the last target frame of the effective s=10 window. The s=11 boundary window has dt=0 and contributes no gradient. The dashed line is the median; on GeoSim-Plume1 it is exactly 8.000 Myr for every trajectory, on GeoSim-Plume2 it varies and the spread is recorded here.
